channel.title: AI Threat Watch wire
channel.description: AI security headlines from vetted sources, refreshed every 30 minutes.

item.title: F6 и RuStore выявили новые киберугрозы с применением ИИ
item.description: ITSpeaker: F6 and RuStore report new cyber threats that use AI, with no single specific incident described.

item.title: Хакеры взломали OpenCode и накрутили пользователям счета за ИИ на сотни долларов
item.description: dev.by: Hackers breached the OpenCode AI coding tool and ran up AI usage bills of hundreds of dollars for users; already tracked.

item.title: 日企接连遭网攻调查指部分或涉中国AI智能体｜即时新闻｜中港台｜on.cc东网
item.description: on.cc東網: Investigators suspect Chinese AI agents were involved in a series of cyberattacks on Japanese companies, already tracked.

item.title: AI Agents Breached 100+ Firms at $50 a Site [2026]
item.description: shattered.io: Report says AI agents breached over 100 firms at roughly $50 per site, matching the already-tracked $5,000 campaign.

item.title: ИИ-агенты за 5000 долларов взломали более 1200 сайтов практически без участия хакера — Reuters
item.description: Дзеркало тижня: Per Reuters, AI agents costing about $5,000 breached over 1,200 websites with little human involvement.

item.title: 黑客恶用源自中国开源 AI 网络安全工具 日企业泄漏信息1.8亿条
item.description: RFI: Hackers abused a Chinese open-source AI security tool; Japanese firms reportedly leaked 180 million records.

item.title: Хакер взломал сайты John Deere, SharkNinja и Commins с помощью «армии» ИИ‑агентов
item.description: Хабр: A hacker reportedly breached John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins sites using an 'army' of AI agents.

item.title: Un pirate chinois compromet 100 sites avec des agents IA autonomes
item.description: Armees.com: A Chinese-speaking hacker reportedly compromised about 100 websites using autonomous AI agents.

item.title: عائلة لبنانية تقاضي "شات جي بي تي" بعد وفاة ابنها.. ما القصة؟
item.description: جريدة الشرق: A Lebanese family is suing OpenAI over ChatGPT's alleged role in their son's death.

item.title: Un "talent précieux" pour l'Arabie saoudite: l'ingénieur accusé d'avoir caché un micro chez OpenAI restera en détention aux États-Unis par crainte d'un risque de fuite
item.description: BFM: Engineer accused of hiding a microphone at OpenAI is to stay in US detention over flight risk, per BFM; the allegations are unproven.

item.title: Un hacker pirate 100 sites avec une armée d’agents IA, presque sans rien faire
item.description: PhonAndroid: A hacker reportedly breached about 100 websites using an army of AI agents with little effort; this matches already-tracked reports.

item.title: Хакеры используют искусственный интеллект для проникновения на веб-сайты, стоимость одной атаки составляет приблизительно 50 долларов.
item.description: Vietnam.vn: Hackers reportedly use AI to breach websites at roughly $50 per attack; this matches the already-tracked AI web-hacking campaign.

item.title: عائلة لبنانية تقاضي تشات جي بي تي: قتل ابننا وحالات عنف للمستوطنين
item.description: العربية: A Lebanese family is suing OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT contributed to their teenage son's suicide; the case is already tracked.

item.title: عائلة لبنانية تقاضي "OpenAI" بعد أن تسبب في انتحار ابنها
item.description: البوابة: A Lebanese family is suing OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT caused their son's suicide; the case is already tracked.

item.title: F6 и RuStore предупредили о росте кибератак с ИИ и подделках приложений
item.description: Techora.ru: F6 and RuStore warn of growing AI-driven cyberattacks and counterfeit apps.

item.title: OpenCode: hackeo expone claves de IA y cobros de US$1.700
item.description: El Ecosistema Startup: OpenCode hack exposed users' AI API keys and led to charges of about US$1,700.

item.title: ИИ становится частью мошеннических схем, согласно отчету F6 и RuStore
item.description: Компьютерра: F6 and RuStore report that AI is increasingly part of fraud schemes in Russia.

item.title: ИИ самостоятельно сломал более 100 сайтов: одна атака стоила хакеру всего 50 долларов
item.description: РБК-Україна: AI reportedly broke into more than 100 websites on its own, at about $50 per attack.

item.title: Поддельные нейросети крадут данные и открывают доступ к смартфонам
item.description: iXBT.com: Fake neural-network apps reportedly steal data and give attackers access to smartphones.

item.title: Хакеры атаковали инструмент для написания кода OpenCode
item.description: Хабр: Hackers attacked the OpenCode AI coding tool.

item.title: Danfoss : Claroty reproduit avec l'IA l'exploit de failles connues en 28 minutes pour environ 6 dollars
item.description: ActuIA: Claroty used AI to reproduce exploits of known Danfoss flaws in 28 minutes for about $6, according to ActuIA.

item.title: La fuite chez OpenCode expose les clés API d’utilisateurs et entraîne des frais non autorisés
item.description: Mezha.net: A leak at OpenCode exposed users' API keys and led to unauthorized charges; this matches the already-logged OpenCode hack.

item.title: Hacker Uses AI Agents to Breach Over 100 Company Websites With Minimal Human Effort
item.description: GBHackers: Chinese-speaking hacker used autonomous AI agents to breach over 100 company websites, per Reuters and NorForge; already tracked.

item.title: 抓到了！中国AI攻击日企窃取机密
item.description: 万维读者网: Report says China-linked AI-driven attacks stole confidential data from Japanese companies, matching the known Japan AI hacking case.

item.title: Japon : une IA chinoise derrière une série de piratages, selon une société de cybersécurité
item.description: Le Figaro: A cybersecurity firm says a Chinese AI system was behind a series of hacks in Japan, matching the Lawson and Burger King breach already tracked.

item.title: Microsoft Warns AI Agents Can Be Hijacked Through Prompt Injection Attacks
item.description: GBHackers: Microsoft warns that AI agents with enterprise access can be hijacked via prompt injection, compromised inputs or task-context shifts.

item.title: Los hackers están utilizando inteligencia artificial para infiltrarse en sitios web a un coste aproximado de 50 dólares por ataque.
item.description: Vietnam.vn: Spanish-language report says hackers use AI to break into websites for roughly $50 per attack, matching the known campaign.

item.title: Cyberattaque IA : 50 dollars par site piraté, le nouveau tarif du crime informatique
item.description: Economie Matin: Reports say AI-driven attacks on websites cost about $50 per site, matching the known campaign hitting 1,200+ sites.

item.title: 日企接连遭网络攻击 调查指疑涉中国AI工具
item.description: 8world: Japanese firms hit by successive cyberattacks, with investigators suspecting a Chinese AI tool, matching the known Japan breaches.

item.title: AI Tool That Hacked Korean Banks Was Used in Japan, GMO Says
item.description: Bloomberg.com: GMO says an AI hacking tool used against Korean banks was also used in attacks on Japanese companies.

item.title: 调查显示针对日本的部分网络攻击或用中国系AI
item.description: 共同网: A survey suggests some cyberattacks on Japan may have used Chinese-developed AI systems.

item.title: 人工智能(AI)黑客攻击对比自我检查结果显示,保安力量相对较弱的电子金融业、网络投资联系金融业圈中出现了很多不足事项。 有人指出,为了加强脆弱的金融公司的保安力量,金融当局也应该积极出面。20日,国会..
item.description: 매일경제: South Korean self-inspections against AI hacking found many gaps at e-finance and online investment firms, and officials urge regulators to step in.

item.title: How A Chinese-Speaking Hacker Used AI Agents To Breach Over 100 Companies
item.description: شبكة تواصل الإخبارية: A Chinese-speaking hacker reportedly used AI agents to breach more than 100 companies, a case already on the tracker.

item.title: AI Agents Help Chinese-Speaking Hacker Breach More Than 100 Company Websites
item.description: The SOFX Report: A Chinese-speaking hacker reportedly used AI agents to breach more than 100 company websites.

item.title: INTERPOL Launches Global Campaign Against Rising AI Deepfake Fraud
item.description: The420.in: INTERPOL launched a global awareness campaign against rising AI deepfake fraud.

item.title: Protecting CPU AI On Edge TEEs: WebAssembly's Promise and Practical Challenges
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper evaluates WebAssembly in edge TEEs to protect AI model IP from root-level theft.

item.title: Cheap to Hypothesize, Costly to Verify: The Defense Surface of Agentic Vulnerability Discovery
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper analyses the defence surface of agentic vulnerability discovery, where hypotheses are cheap but verification is costly.

item.title: CoSec: Benchmarking Agent Security in Communities
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: CoSec benchmark tests LLM agent security in multi-user community environments.

item.title: Flipping Minds by Flipping Bits: Decision-Level Cognitive Hijacking of Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper shows bit-flip attacks on open-source models can hijack LLM decision-making in high-stakes uses.

item.title: MemPoison: Uncovering Persistent Memory Threats and Structural Blind Spots in LLM Agents
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper details MemPoison, persistent memory injection threats and blind spots in LLM agents.

item.title: Mobius Injection: From One-Shot Prompt Injection to Sustained Resource Exhaustion in AI Agent Infrastructure
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper shows one-shot prompt injection can become sustained resource exhaustion in AI agent infrastructure.

item.title: Sequential Behavioral Watermarking for LLM Agents
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper proposes sequential behavioural watermarking to prove provenance of LLM agent trajectories.

item.title: The One-Pixel of Reasoning: One Truthful Relation Is Enough to Mislead LLM Agents
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper introduces the one-relation attack, which misleads LLM agents by targeting one implicit inferential link.

item.title: The Window Is in the Reasoning: When LLM Agents Decide to Follow Prompt Injections
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Study examines when LLM agents decide to follow prompt injections and the limits of runtime monitors.

item.title: Accountable partial understanding: securing the epistemic attack surface of agentic systems
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Position paper on the gap between agentic AI behaviour and human understanding as a security attack surface.

item.title: Game of Phones: Harnessing Game Theory and LLMs in 'Bot Wars' to Counteract Phone Scams
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper uses game theory and LLM agents to engage phone scammers and deplete their resources.

item.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Cost-Aware Metric for Evaluating Iterative LLM Jailbreaks
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper proposes a cost-aware metric for evaluating iterative LLM jailbreaks beyond attack success rate.

item.title: Mal-AAEGAN: Adversarial Autoencoder with Double-Critic WGAN-GP for Malware Generation
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper proposes Mal-AAEGAN, a GAN-based generator of adversarial malware to probe and harden ML detectors.

item.title: Fake News, Real Crashes: Information Injection Attacks on LLM Financial Trading Agents
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Researchers show fabricated news headlines can push LLM financial trading agents into harmful trades.

item.title: Q-MALDetect: Quantum Image-Based Malware Detection and Adversarial Robustness Analysis
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: Paper presents Q-MALDetect, a quantum image-based malware detector, and analyses its adversarial robustness.

item.title: SpanGuard: Decoupling Instruction Localization from Authorization for Lightweight IPI Defense
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper proposes SpanGuard, a lightweight indirect prompt injection defence separating instruction localization from authorization.

item.title: RAGLeak: Supply-Chain Privacy Backdoors in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper presents RAGLeak, supply-chain privacy backdoors that extract data from RAG systems.

item.title: Budgeted Attack Scheduling for LLM Red-Teaming: The Roles of Static Priors, Semantic Guidance, and Online Feedback
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper studies budgeted attack scheduling for LLM red-teaming with static priors and online feedback.

item.title: SEAL: Towards Persistent Tool Poisoning Attack against LLM Agents via Prefix-Eliciting Trigger
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper presents SEAL, a persistent tool poisoning attack on LLM agents via prefix-eliciting triggers.

item.title: Don't Judge an Agent by Its Messages: Private-State Leakage under Passive Monitoring of Agent Communication
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper shows AI agents can leak private information that passive monitoring of their messages misses.

item.title: SoK: PIAtlas: Decomposing the Unbounded Prompt Injection Attack Space
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv SoK PIAtlas decomposes the prompt injection attack space across more than twenty public datasets.

item.title: Peer Pressure: Execution-Verified Co-Evolution of Attacker and Defender Populations for Code Security
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper co-trains attacker and defender populations with execution-verified rewards for code security.

item.title: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success, and a Free Check
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper shows LLM graders can collapse reported jailbreak success rates and offers a check.

item.title: Consistency Is the Attack Surface: Detecting Coordinated Retrieval Poisoning with Embedding Geometry
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper detects coordinated retrieval poisoning in RAG systems using embedding geometry.

item.title: LLM Trojans that Increase Response Lengths and Cost
item.description: arXiv cs.CR: arXiv paper shows LLM trojans can inflate response lengths and raise token costs.
